summary: A 1942 spruce lookout in San Juan National Forest replaced in 1964 by a 55-ft timber tower; staffed into the 1970s, saved from demolition by a volunteer foundation in 1991, now a popular rental.

facts.design: 55-ft treated-timber tower with a 15'x15' live-in cab

access.note: Operated under permit by the Jersey Jim Foundation; key pickup and waiver required at P&D Grocery.

visit.trail_note: Deck is 55 feet above ground via steep stairs; rental includes overnight stays, capped at 4 people.

events.note: Original tower built of local spruce
Replaced with current 55-ft treated timber tower and 15'x15' cab
Tower was slated for demolition; renovated and saved by the Jersey Jim Foundation, a local volunteer nonprofit, which now operates it under permit

evidence.supports: built 1942 of spruce; replaced 1964 with 55-ft tower and 15x15 cab
evidence.quote: A landmark in the mountains of southwest Colorado since 1942, Jersey Jim Lookout is located on the San Juan National Forest at an elevation of nearly 10,000 feet. The original tower, constructed of local spruce, was replaced with a 55' treated timber tower with a large 15'X15' live-in cab in 1964.
The Jersey Jim Lookout Tower was home to U.S. Forest Service fire lookouts from the 1940s to 1970s.

evidence.supports: 1991 renovation by Jersey Jim Foundation, saved from demolition, operates under permit
evidence.quote: The tower was renovated and saved from demolition in 1991 by the Jersey Jim Foundation, a nonprofit local volunteer organization, which operates and maintains the tower under permit with the San Juan National Forest.

evidence.supports: 2019 condition report: tower good, cab excellent
evidence.quote: According to a 2019 report, the condition of tower is good and the cab exterior and roof are in excellent condition. Condition of cab interior is excellent.
The Jersey Jim Lookout Tower is named after an early cattleman who ran Jersey cattle in the area. Today, cattle are still grazed in the area under permit.

evidence.supports: original furniture, propane systems, no electricity/water
evidence.quote: The Tower cab includes the original furniture and propane heating and lighting. However, there is no electricity or running water.

evidence.supports: historic fire finder still present for guest use
evidence.quote: In the middle of the cab is the historic fire finder, which early lookouts used to spot fires, and which you can use to orient yourself to surrounding landmarks.

evidence.supports: 4-person overnight cap, key pickup at P&D Grocery with waiver
evidence.quote: Overnight stay is restricted to a maximum of 4 (four) persons, including at least one adult over 21 years of age

evidence.supports: deck safety: 55 ft high, trap door, lightning rules
evidence.quote: Steep stairs, Trap Door on Deck, Deck is 55 feet above ground, Lightning Storms

sources.title: Jersey Jim Fire Tower, San Juan National Forest
